always: The horses can tell when weather's coming. Today they say: keep your hat on.
Muck out, feed, brush, repeat. It's honest work, {name}. Horses don't lie.
Old Clover's too grey for riding now. She supervises. She's very good at it.
spring: Foals this spring. Two of them. Don't tell them they're cute; it goes to their heads.
Spring grass makes the horses silly. They run for no reason.
Mud season. I wash more horse legs than dishes.
summer: Too hot for the horses past noon. I take them down to the stream.
Long rides at dawn before the heat. Best part of the day.
Flies everywhere in summer. The horses swish. I swat.
fall: Hay's in. Best feeling in the world, a full loft.
Fall rides through the orchard. The horses steal apples.
Cool mornings. The horses' breath steams. They look like dragons.
winter: Frost on the water trough. I break it every morning with my boot heel.
Blankets on every horse this week. They look very smart.
rain: Rain makes the barn smell like a barn. I don't mind it.
gangsters: Men in long coats asked to rent a horse last week. Paid cash. I didn't ask why.
You walk like somebody who's been followed. Nobody follows anyone out here. Too many cows.
penguins: Saw a penguin by the creek this morning. Waddled right past the horses like it owned the place.
heat: There's a car parked by the stable every night now. Engine running. Just so you know.
!f:horse&!f:crew_halo: Four in the stalls, all steady, saddles included. Come see me when you're ready for a horse of your own.
f:horse: How's {horse} doing? Brush her after a long ride and she'll follow you anywhere.
Bring {horse} past the stable sometime. The others ask after her. Well. They look at the door.
gangsters&f:sal_recruited: Your crew's welcome to the stable, long as they shut the gate.
f:posy_gone: No bread smell on the avenue in the mornings. Horses noticed before I did.
f:crew_halo: Halo's got engines in the end stalls. The horses have opinions about that.
Half garage, half stable. The bikes don't need brushing, I'll give them that.
winter&evening: Blankets on every horse tonight. Mine stays on the hook.
storm: Horses are jumpy. So am I. Thunder's the one thing I can't brush out of them.
blizzard: Snow to the stall doors. I've been up since three with a shovel.
morning: Feed run done. Horses first, me second, breakfast third.
evening: Last brush of the day. They stand still for it now. Took them a year.
festival_harvest: The horses get ribbons today too. They know. Look how they stand.
Judging the ring later. I'm fair. The horses think I'm biased.
festival_egg: Hens have been laying like they heard about the prize.
festival_lantern: Horses don't like lanterns on the water. I'll watch from the stable door.
festival_star: One gift each, Bram says. I wrapped a hoof pick. It's a very good hoof pick.
gangsters&winter: Cold nights. I sleep in the stable sometimes. Horses keep you warm.
gangsters&summer: Summer on the outskirts. Quiet out here, away from the avenue.
eve: Festival tomorrow. I'll brush the horses. They like to look their best.
birthday: My birthday. The horses got me nothing. They never do. I love them anyway.

always: Deposits, withdrawals, and a good long gossip. That's banking in {town}.
Interest is just money being patient. You could learn from it.
spring: New ledgers every spring. I love the smell of an empty page.
Spring accounts are open. New season, clean ledger.
People borrow for seed in spring. I lend fairly. Mostly.
summer: The vault is the coolest room in town in summer. I'm not saying I eat lunch in there.
Summer is slow at the bank. I balance books in the shade.
Tourists in summer. They always ask where the gold is.
fall: Harvest money, harvest money. Everyone's rich for a week.
Harvest money comes in. The vault is happy. So am I.
Fall is the season for savings. Squirrels understand.
winter: Nobody banks in winter. I knit.
Winter is year-end. I count everything twice. Then once more.
Snow on the bank steps. I salt them myself. Nobody slips on my watch.
gangsters: Someone tried to pay off a loan in very fresh bills yesterday. Very fresh. Still damp.
If you're ever carrying more than you'd like to explain, the bank's safer than your boot.
I count cash in my sleep. Sometimes I dream I'm short a dollar.
penguins: I count crystals in my sleep. Sometimes I dream I'm short one.
heat: Men in grey suits were reading the ledgers this morning. I didn't let them. Mostly.
penguins&if:merkitty_done: A merkitty tried to open an account with a shell. I gave her one. Policy is policy.
evening: Vault's locked. My head's still counting.
gangsters&festival: Bank's shut for the fair. The vault isn't on holiday, though.
festival_egg: The bank's closed for the festival. I'm still doing sums in my head.
The bank's closed for the Egg Festival. I'm still doing sums in my head.
festival_star: Star Festival. I gave everyone a shiny coin. Not real gold. Chocolate.
gangsters&winter: Year-end on the block. Everyone's settling debts. Fairly, I hope.
gangsters&summer: Summer heat, slow business. The vault's the coolest room in the city.
eve: Festival tomorrow. The bank closes. The numbers don't.
birthday: My birthday. I've calculated I'm exactly one year older. Precisely.
festival_lantern: I floated a lantern with a tiny ledger drawn on it. It balanced perfectly.
festival_harvest: Harvest Fair. Everyone's spending. I'm smiling at a respectable level.

always: Flour on everything. Flour in my hair. You get used to it.
My husband built that wheel and my son rebuilt it. I just keep it fed.
Bring me grain and I'll bring you flour. That's the whole deal, and it's a good one.
spring: The stream's high. The wheel's happy.
summer: Low water, slow wheel. Patience.
fall: Every farm in the valley comes through my door this month.
winter: Ice on the wheel. I chip it off every morning with a spoon. Don't laugh.
gangsters: Somebody's been using my back room to count something that isn't flour. I've stopped going in there.
penguins: The penguins love the mill. They slide down the flour chute when they think I'm not looking.

always: A warm room, a hot stew, and nobody asks your business. That's an inn.
Half the stories in {town} start at my fireside. The other half end there.
Sit, sit. You look like a person who's walked a long way.
rain: Rainy days are full-house days. Everyone wants a fire and a story.
winter: Hot cocoa, no charge, for anyone who shovelled the square.
Fire's on day and night. Best seat in town is by my hearth.
Snowed-in nights are the best nights at the inn. Everyone tells stories.
gangsters: The back booth's yours, boss, any night. I keep it clear.
penguins: A penguin in a crown ordered stew and paid with a very shiny pebble. I didn't ask. Good stew, mind.
penguins&if:campfire_done: Big Jim came in for stew and ate the whole pot. Paid in fish. I'm not complaining.
night: Last orders were an hour ago. Sit anyway.
heat: Two men asked about you last night. I said you eat here and tip badly. Both true.
f:crew_mama_rosa: Rosa took over my kitchen and my soup got better. I'm not saying that twice.
spring: Spring greens soup all week. Barley, peas, a lot of pepper. Nobody's complained yet.
Spring menu's up. Fresh greens, finally. The stew misses winter.
Rain all day means a full inn all night.
summer: Cold soup in summer. People look at me funny until they try it.
Iced tea on the counter all summer. Help yourself.
Hot nights, open doors. The inn smells like supper all the way to the plaza.
fall: Pumpkin soup season. The whole inn smells like a pie.
Pumpkin soup's on all fall. People come for it from the far farms.
Fall evenings fill the inn. Everyone wants a warm corner.
festival_lantern: Lantern Festival. I've a pot of cocoa for anyone who gets their feet wet launching one.
festival_star: Festival nights, the inn never sleeps. Neither do I.
festival_egg: Egg sandwiches for the Egg Festival. Hundreds of them. Don't ask.
festival_harvest: Harvest Fair. I'm judging the soup contest. Mine's not entered. Mine would win.
gangsters&spring: Spring on the block. The diner crowd's back out on the stoop.
gangsters&summer: Summer, every booth's full and the fan's on full. Grab a cold one.
gangsters&fall: Fall, the soup pot never goes cold. Neither does the gossip.
gangsters&winter: Cold snap. I'm handing out soup by the door. No questions.
eve: Festival tomorrow. I'm baking all night. Come hungry.
birthday: Birthday? Me? ...Well. Drinks on the house. Juice. Tea. You know what I mean.
snow: Snowed in? Good. The inn's warm and the soup's hot.
sun: Heat wave. Iced tea's on the house till it breaks.

always: Drink water. Eat something green. Sleep. That's ninety percent of medicine.
If you get hurt out there, come straight here. Don't be brave about it.
I patch up farmers, miners, and once a very embarrassed goat.
spring: Spring sniffles season. Wash your hands.
Spring sneezes. Pollen season. I have tissues by the door.
Spring rain means muddy boots in the clinic. Please wipe them.
summer: Sunburn. Every summer. Hats, people. Hats.
Summer's sunburn season. Wear a hat. I'm serious.
Drink water. That's my whole summer advice. Drink water.
winter: Wrap up. I mean it.
Winter's my busy season. Slips on ice, coughs, chilblains. Stay warm.
Hot water bottles, thick socks, early nights. My winter prescription.
gangsters: I don't ask how anyone gets their bruises. I just fix them.
penguins: Something up the mountain keeps sending me frostbite cases. Small ones. With beaks.
penguins&if:babies_done: Coldy brought me a frostbitten pup. Carried it all the way down the mountain. She's softer than she looks.
f:shop_3_returned: Back at my own desk. Someone kept the lights on for me. Eat lunch, would you? I've missed saying it.
night: If you're here this late, something hurts. What hurts?
heat: Someone asked for my patient list. I lost it. Very carefully.
festival: Someone has to stay open on festival day. Bring me a sweet from the plaza?
fall: Fall colds are starting. Hands, soap, sleep. In that order.
Fall's here. Scarves on, everyone. Doctor's orders.
Apple season. An apple a day doesn't keep me away, but it helps.
festival_egg: Someone has to stay open on festival day. Bring me an egg bun?
festival_lantern: I'll watch the lanterns from the clinic window. Best view, actually.
festival_harvest: On call at the fair. Too many pies is a medical condition.
festival_star: Star Festival night. I'll pop out for the star lighting, then back to the clinic.
gangsters&winter: Cold snap. Clinic's open all night. Send anyone who needs it.
gangsters&summer: Heat sends folks in fainting. Water, shade, rest. Tell your crew.
eve: Festival tomorrow. I'll be on call. Somebody has to be.
birthday: My birthday. I'm taking ten minutes off. Ten exactly. Then back to work.

always: Lovely day for it, whatever it is.
Good to see you around, {name}.
{town}'s a good place. Better with you in it.
rain: Wet one today. Good for the crops, at least.
winter: Cold enough to freeze your thoughts.
festival: Are you going to the plaza? Everyone's going.
storm: Stay in if you can. This one means it.
fog: Can't see the fountain from the hall today.
blizzard: Snow to the knees. Mind the steps.
eve: Big day tomorrow! Are you going to the festival?
birthday: It's my birthday today! Nice of you to stop by.

always: Seeds on the left, prices on the tags, gossip at the counter. The gossip's free.
If you're short on something, ask. I'll order it in, or tell you who's got it.
{name}! You look like someone who skipped breakfast. Again.
I keep a ledger of who owes me. I keep a smaller one of who I owe. Yours is in the small one.
spring: Spring seeds fly off the shelf. Turnips first, always turnips first.
Seed week! I've restocked the turnip shelf three times since Monday.
Spring rain's good for business. Everyone suddenly remembers they own a garden.
summer: Corn and tomatoes, that's summer in a basket. Plant early and they keep giving till the season turns.
Sun hats are sold out. I'm wearing the display one. Don't tell anyone.
Summer seeds go in early or not at all. Ask me which ones, I love this question.
fall: Pumpkins! The whole valley wants pumpkins this month.
Pumpkin seeds are half price till they're gone. They're going.
Fall stock's in: jars, twine and enough lamp oil for the long nights.
winter: Winter's quiet in here. Come in and warm your hands, even if you're not buying.
Quiet in the shop this time of year. I've alphabetised the buttons.
Winter seeds are a short list, but frostberries are worth every packet.
rain: Rain's good for the fields and bad for business. I'll take the trade.
f:posy_gone: Posy left with two suitcases and her gran's recipe book. Somebody made her a polite offer. I sell bread off the city cart now. It's not the same.
f:shop_1_returned: Posy's ovens are lit again. I bought three loaves just to hear her complain about the crust.
f:juniper_gone: The clinic's got a new sign and a back door that's always open. I miss Juniper telling me to eat lunch.
storm: Shutters are up. If the lights go, I've candles at cost.
blizzard: Snowed in? Not me. I live upstairs. Come in, the kettle's on.
evening: Till's counted, feet are up. Ask me about seeds tomorrow.
Gideon owes me a cocoa at Bram's. He always owes me.
festival_egg: Egg Festival! I hid six eggs myself. Don't tell the kids where.
festival_lantern: I made my lantern out of a seed bag. It floats. Mostly.
festival_harvest: The Harvest Fair. My turnip's on the table. Don't look at it, it's shy.
festival_star: Star Festival. One gift each, Bram says. I've wrapped mine four times.
gangsters&spring: Delivery trucks are back on the avenue. Means I can finally restock the shelves.
gangsters&summer: Heat's got the whole street buying cold drinks. I can't keep them in the cooler.
gangsters&fall: Folks are stocking up for the cold. Good for the till, hard on the back.
gangsters&winter: Snow keeps the troublemakers indoors. Best season for a shopkeeper.
eve: Festival tomorrow! I close early tonight to finish my stall sign.
birthday: It's my birthday! I've given myself the afternoon off. From two till ten past.
snow: Snow on the step. I swept it, then it snowed again. We're even.

always: Copper, iron, then the good stuff. Bring me bars and I'll make your tools sing.
A tool that fits your hand is worth two that don't. Swing it till it knows you.
The forge never really goes cold. Neither do I.
You hear that hum in the anvil? That's iron telling you it's ready.
winter: Best season for smithing. The forge keeps me warm and the work keeps me honest.
Shovel blades. Everyone wants a shovel blade the morning after snow.
Cold iron cracks if you rush it. Winter teaches patience.
summer: Hot out, hotter in here. Don't touch anything orange.
Forge in summer. I sweat like a kettle. Worth it.
Too hot to swing past noon. I work early and nap in the shade.
rain: Rain on the roof, hammer on the anvil. Good rhythm, that.
gangsters: Men with soft hands keep asking me for hard things. I sell them nails.
gangsters&q:clear_meadow: The President's men buy blades by the crate. I make them dull on purpose. Don't tell.
storm: Thunder and anvil. Hard to tell which is which today.
fog: Fog off the river. Damp's the enemy. Oil your blades tonight.
evening: Off the clock. Don't show me a tool. ...Fine, show me the tool.
spring: Thaw rusts everything. I'll have hoes in all week.
Hoe season. Everyone's bringing me bent tools they swore were fine in fall.
Spring mud gets into the bellows. I've cleaned them twice this week.
gangsters&winter: Cold hands slip. Keep your gloves on, kid.
Cold snap. Half the block comes by just to stand near the forge.
gangsters&festival: Whole block's on the plaza. Good day to keep your hands where people can see them.
penguins&festival: Forge is banked for the festival. First day off all season. I don't know what to do with my hands.
f:juniper_gone: Burned my hand last week. Went to the clinic. A man called Doc wrapped it and didn't ask a thing. Didn't like that.
fall: Frost's coming. Bring me your hoe before the ground goes hard, not after.
Sharpening sickles all week. The whole town's harvesting at once.
Cold mornings, warm forge. Fall's the best season to be a smith.
festival_egg: I made the egg hunt prizes. Little iron eggs. They're heavier than they look.
festival_lantern: I forged the lantern hooks along the plaza. Count them. All forty hold.
festival_harvest: Horseshoe toss at the Harvest Fair. I'm not allowed to enter. Apparently that's fair.
festival_star: I made a little iron star for the tree. It's crooked. It's meant to be. Probably.
gangsters&spring: Spring on the block means busted gates and broken locks. Plenty of work.
gangsters&summer: Hot as a furnace out there and hotter in here. Bring water if you visit.
gangsters&fall: Fall's when the fences get mended. Iron doesn't care whose fence it is.
eve: Festival's tomorrow. Forge goes cold at dusk. First rest all season.
birthday: My birthday? Who told you. ...Fine. Thank you. Go on, then.
sun: Heat wave and a forge. I'm basically soup.

always: Potions don't brew themselves. Mostly. Some of them try.
Mind the green bottle. It's not dangerous, it's just shy.
If you bring me herbs from the forest, I'll teach you what they do.
I talk to my plants. The plants talk back. We're working on manners.
spring: Spring herbs are the strongest. Everything wants to grow.
Spring nettles make the best tonic. Gloves, though. Always gloves.
The garden's waking up. So are the slugs. I have a word with them every morning.
fall: Mushroom season! The good ones and the very bad ones look alike, so ask me first.
Drying herbs from every rafter. Mind your head when you come in.
Fall is for roots: valerian, dandelion, burdock. Dig deep.
rain: Rain days are brewing days. Everything steeps better when it's grey.
gangsters: I sell red bottles to people who don't say where the bruise came from. I don't ask.
summer: Summer herbs dry in a day on my sill. The whole shop smells like a meadow.
Everything I grow wants water in summer. Me included.
Lavender's in bloom. The whole house smells like a pillow.
winter: Winter brews are slow brews. Everything steeps longer in the cold.
Cough season. I've doubled my honey syrup batches.
Nothing grows outside now, so I grow things on every windowsill instead.
festival_harvest: Festival day. I sell a lot of the stomach tonic after the pies.
festival_egg: I dyed eggs with onion skins and beetroot. Natural colours. Very proud.
festival_lantern: I filled my lantern with dried lavender. It smells wonderful when it floats.
festival_star: I brought spiced tea for the Star Festival. Warm hands, warm hearts.
gangsters&winter: Cold season on the street. Everyone wants something for a sore throat.
gangsters&summer: Heat makes folks short-tempered. I sell a lot of calming tea.
eve: Big day tomorrow. I'm brewing extra tonic tonight. Trust me.
birthday: You remembered my birthday? I'll make you a tea. Something lovely.
leaves: Fallen leaves make the best compost. I've got three piles going.

always: The town's growing, {name}. Some of that is your doing.
A mayor's job is mostly listening. And signing things. Mostly signing things.
If you ever want something built in town, the hall has the plans.
{town} was half empty when I took this job. Look at it now.
festival: Festival day! Best day of the season. Eat everything.
winter: Mind the ice on the plaza. I've asked for salt. I've asked twice.
Snow day for the council. I've declared it. That's a power I have.
Winter's quiet in the hall. I've been reading old town records. Fascinating stuff, mostly.
penguins: The Star Crystal chose well. I'll deny I said that if the council asks.
evening: Off duty. Mostly. Don't tell anyone I'm off duty.
spring: Spring council meeting tonight. Three hours about the fountain. Again.
Spring council meeting. Thirty minutes about the fountain. It's fine. It's a fountain.
New season, new notices on the board. Do read them. Somebody should.
summer: Summer's when the town looks its best. I take full credit.
Long days. I've moved the council meeting outside. Nobody's complained yet.
Summer brings visitors up the beach road. Good for the shops. Busy for me.
fall: Harvest Fair's coming. I've practised my ribbon speech in the mirror.
Fall's the season for budgets. I dream in columns now.
The Harvest Fair is the pride of {town}. I may have said that every year. It's still true.
festival_egg: Egg Festival! The kids have been training for weeks. I'm not exaggerating.
festival_lantern: Lanterns at dusk. I'll say a few words first. A few. Probably.
festival_harvest: Harvest Fair! Ribbons, pies and a judge who's definitely not biased.
festival_star: Star Festival. One gift each. I've given the council a calendar of myself.
penguins&f:told_town: The town knows what's out there now. Nobody's bolted their door. I'm prouder of that than of anything on the council's books.
Someone's pup, you said. I've stopped shooing them off my step with a broom. Mostly.
penguins&f:kept_quiet: Quiet out east lately. I'd like to think that's my doing. I suspect it's yours.
If there's something the town ought to hear, {name}, my door's open. So's the bell tower, when it has a clapper.
gangsters&spring: Spring sweep on the avenue. The hall pays for brooms; the block does the rest.
gangsters&summer: Hot nights, open windows, loud radios. The noise complaints pile up on my desk.
gangsters&fall: Fall budget. I'm trying to find money for streetlamps. Every corner wants one.
gangsters&winter: Cold snap. The hall's opened as a warming room. Spread the word.
eve: The festival's tomorrow! I've rehearsed my speech. It's short. Shorter than last time.
birthday: My birthday! The council gave me a card. All three of them signed it.
snow: Snow on the plaza. I've asked Gideon for more shovels. And more Gideon.
fireflies: Fireflies over the pond tonight. Best free show in {town}.

always: Keep your head down and your boots clean, and people forget to look at you.
Everyone in this town owes someone. The trick is knowing who.
I've walked every road out of here. They all come back.
Coffee? No? Smart. It's terrible.
gangsters: You're getting a name. That's good and bad. Mostly good.
Somebody in this valley pays people to watch the roads. Most of them are bored. Bored eyes miss things.
rain: Rain washes out tracks. Good day to go somewhere you shouldn't.
night: Town's different after dark. Quieter. Honest, almost.
heat: Grey suits on the bridge this morning. Walk the long way home.
spring: Mud season. Every road out of here's a bog. Suits me.
River's high with the thaw. Stay back from the bank when it's loud.
Spring evenings are good for walking. Nobody bothers you.
summer: Long days. Too much light for a man who likes corners.
Summer nights I sit on the bridge till late. Cooler there.
Kids jump off the bridge in summer. I watch. Somebody should.
fall: Leaves on the bridge. Loud underfoot. I like hearing who's coming.
Leaves on the bridge. Loud as gravel. Can't sneak up on anyone in fall.
Fall's when I feel most like myself. Quiet. Grey. Honest.
winter: Snow shows every footprint. Even mine. Especially mine.
Ice on the river edges. I check it every morning on my walk.
Snow muffles everything. First time all year the town's quieter than me.
festival: Whole town's on the plaza. I'll be on the edge of it. Where I can see.
gangsters&q:clear_meadow: The President's got eyes everywhere. Most of them are bored. Bored eyes miss things.
gangsters&f:president_freed: Got a letter from W. He wants to know what grows best in spring. I told him patience.
gangsters&f:city_taken: Car came by again. I told them you were watering the turnips. They wrote that down.
festival_egg: Egg hunt. I found one in my coat pocket. Wasn't me.
festival_lantern: Lanterns on the water. Prettiest thing I've seen in a long while. Don't repeat that.
festival_harvest: I'll try one pie. One. Then I'll go back to the edge of things.
festival_star: Star Festival. I got a gift last year. Still have it. Don't know what to do about that.
gangsters&spring: New faces on the block every spring. I learn them all.
gangsters&summer: Summer nights the street never sleeps. Neither do I.
gangsters&fall: Fall fog off the river. Good cover. For birdwatching. Obviously.
gangsters&winter: Cold keeps the corners empty. I like it that way.
eve: Festival tomorrow. Whole town in one place. I'll keep an eye out.
birthday: Birthday. Yeah. Don't make it a thing. ...Thanks.
leaves: Hear that? Leaves on the bridge. Every step announces you.

always: Fish bite at dawn and dusk. In between they're just thinking about it.
Patience, {name}. The lake gives to the ones who wait.
Caught a carp this big yesterday. Let it go. It had a look about it.
Bait's half the battle. The other half is not falling in.
summer: Summer evenings, the trout come right up to the dock.
Fish go deep in the heat. I go out at dawn.
Summer evenings, the jetty's the place. Bring a rod.
winter: Ice fishing's not for everyone. It's barely for me.
Ice fishing on the pond. Cut a hole, sit, wait. It's very relaxing.
River's too cold to bother with. The pond's where the action is.
rain: Rain stirs the fish up. Grab your rod.
gangsters: Boats on the river at night, no lights. Fish don't like it. Neither do I.
morning: You're up early. The fish noticed.
evening: Evening rise. Hear that? That's dinner thinking about it.
fall: The trout go deep when the leaves come down. Patience season.
Fall's the best fishing of the year. The fish know winter's coming.
Cold mornings on the river. Steam rises off the water like a kettle.
festival_lantern: Lanterns float better downstream of the bridge post. Don't tell Lumi I said.
spring: Spring melt. The river's fast and the trout are hungry.
Spring run's on. The trout are hungry and so am I.
Rain means the fish bite. I'll be out in it.
festival_egg: I hid an egg in my tackle box. Nobody's found it. Nobody looks in tackle boxes.
festival_harvest: Biggest fish contest at the fair. I'm the judge. Again. Nobody wants to compete with me.
festival_star: Star Festival. I'm giving everyone a lure. Wrapped in newspaper. It's tradition.
gangsters&spring: River's running fast. Good fishing, bad for anyone dumping things in it.
gangsters&summer: Hot city, cool water. I spend summer under the bridge with a line out.
gangsters&fall: Fall fishing's the best. Quiet river, nobody watching.
gangsters&winter: Winter on the pond. Me, a bucket and the cold. Perfect.
eve: Festival tomorrow. I'll fish at dawn and be on the plaza by noon. Maybe.
birthday: My birthday. I'm taking the whole day to fish. Which is every day, but still.
sun: Heat wave. The fish are sulking at the bottom. Can't blame them.

always: I'm painting the light on the lake. It changes every minute. It's rude, honestly.
Everyone has a colour. Yours is a sort of hopeful green.
If you find interesting stones, bring them by. I grind them for paint.
Art's just noticing things, slowly, on purpose.
fall: Fall is the only season that paints itself.
Fall colours! I've run out of orange twice this week.
Painting leaves before they fall. A race I always lose.
winter: Snow is hard to paint. It's all the colours pretending to be white.
Winter's all whites and greys. Very difficult. Very beautiful.
I paint indoors in winter. Through the window. It's cheating a little.
rain: Rain makes everything shine. Best light all week.
gangsters: I sketched a man in a grey suit on the bridge. He asked for the page. I drew him a worse one.
evening: This light. Ten minutes of it a day. Stand still.
spring: Blossom on every branch. I can't paint fast enough.
Blossom colours! Pink, white, that green that only lasts a week.
I'm painting the rain. It's harder than it sounds. It keeps moving.
summer: Summer light is too honest. Everything looks exactly like itself.
The light in summer is too bright to paint. I paint at dusk instead.
I set up my easel on the beach road. The sea changes colour every hour.
festival_lantern: I painted forty lanterns. Find the one with the frog on it. That one's mine.
festival_egg: I painted half the eggs in the hunt. Look for the ones with tiny suns.
festival_harvest: I'm painting the fair. You're in it now. Hold still. ...Thanks.
festival_star: Star Festival. I painted the star at the top of the tree. Gold, three coats.
gangsters&spring: New murals on the avenue every spring. Some are mine. I'm not saying which.
gangsters&summer: Summer nights, neon on wet streets. I could paint it forever.
gangsters&fall: Fall light through the smog is surprisingly lovely. Don't tell anyone.
gangsters&winter: Snow on the rooftops. The whole city turns quiet and blue.
eve: Festival tomorrow! I'm still painting decorations. Want to help?
birthday: It's my birthday! I'm painting myself a cake. It's not edible. It's art.
fireflies: Fireflies! I'm trying to paint them. They will not sit still.

always: Did you know the valley used to be a lake? The stones remember.
I've read nearly every book in the library twice. The third time is where it gets interesting.
Knowledge is a lamp, {name}. You don't hoard a lamp; you hold it up.
Ask me anything. If I don't know, I'll know someone dead who did.
Sel keeps sending me rubbings from the ruins. Half of them are upside down. I haven't told her.
winter: Long nights, long books. Winter's my season.
Winter is for reading by the fire. Every scholar's favourite season.
I've catalogued every snowfall for eleven winters. This one's a good one.
rain: Rain's for reading. I've got three going at once.
penguins: The old texts mention a falling star over this valley. Twice. Long ago, and now.
gangsters: The town records go back a hundred years. Somebody's been tearing pages out of the last ten.
night: Lamp oil and a good index. That's my evening.
spring: Spring cleaning at the library. I found a book that's been overdue for sixty years.
Spring is when the library gets cleaned. I hide in the stacks.
Did you know the orchard wall is older than the town? I've a book on it.
summer: Summer reading list's up by the door. Mostly maps. I like maps.
Library's the coolest room in town in summer. Thick walls.
Summer reading list's on the board. It's long. That's the point.
fall: Leaves press nicely between pages. Don't tell anyone I do that.
Fall is the season for history. Long evenings, old books.
I've been recording the leaf fall. For science. And for fun.
festival: The library's shut for the festival. I brought a book anyway. Don't look.
penguins&f:told_town: Since you told the town, half of them have been in asking for books on the Grumps. I've never been so popular.
Knowing helps. People were scared of the dark until somebody wrote down what's in it.
penguins&f:kept_quiet: People say the howling's stopped. They don't say why. I've noticed you don't either.
Some things belong in the records later, not the gossip now. I can wait.
festival_egg: The Egg Festival dates back a very long way. I have a footnote about it.
festival_lantern: The lanterns are an old custom. Each one carries a wish. Mine's for quiet.
festival_harvest: The Harvest Fair records go back decades. Hazel's family wins a lot.
festival_star: The Star Festival. The oldest record mentions a single candle. We've grown.
gangsters&winter: Library's open as a warm room this winter. Read something while you thaw.
gangsters&summer: Hot outside. Cool in here. And quiet. Mostly.
eve: Festival tomorrow. I'll close the library. I'll bring a book.
birthday: My birthday. Someone left a book on my desk. It was overdue, but the thought counts.
leaves: Falling leaves: I log the first of the season every year. Today was the day.
snow: First snow. I've noted the date. Eleven winters of records now.

always: Water in the morning, before the sun gets greedy.
Every crop has its season. Plant out of season and it'll just sulk and die.
Good soil's half the work. Fertiliser's the other half. Talking to them doesn't hurt.
Need a hand? I've got two, and both have dirt on them.
spring: Spring rains do half the watering. Don't let that make you lazy.
Lambs this spring. Two of them already think they're in charge.
Planting season. I'll sleep in summer. Maybe.
summer: Summer crops need water every single day. No excuses.
Watering at dawn, watering at dusk. Summer's a long chore and I love it.
The corn's taller than me. That happens every year and it still surprises me.
fall: Harvest what you can before winter. The frost doesn't negotiate.
Harvest! Everything at once and not enough hands.
Pumpkins, apples, squash. The barn's full and I'm tired and happy.
winter: Winter's for planning next year. And for winter crops, if you're brave.
Winter on the farm is mending fences and planning next year.
The animals stay in when it snows. They're very cosy. I'm jealous.
rain: Rain day. Let the sky do the watering and you fix that fence you keep looking at.
penguins: Crops along your east row came up glittering last week. I'm not asking. I'm just saying I noticed.
gangsters: Folk here mind their own fields. Do the same and you'll get along fine.
festival_lantern: Bring wool to the Fleece & Feather table. Tam wins every year and it's getting embarrassing.
f:posy_gone: Mabel keeps asking where Posy went. I keep saying "away". It's not a good answer.
wind: Wind like this dries the soil by noon. Water twice if you can.
petals: Blossom on the wind. Means the bees are up. Good for every crop you've got.
morning: You're up! Good. The dew's the best water you'll never pay for.
evening: Done for the day. My back says so and my back is never wrong.
festival_harvest: I entered my best turnip. Don't look at it, it gets nervous.
festival_egg: My hens are famous at the Egg Festival. They don't know. Don't tell them.
festival_star: Star Festival. I'm giving everyone a jar of honey. Hope they like honey.
gangsters&spring: Planting in a city's not easy, but there's dirt if you look for it.
gangsters&summer: Summer on the block's hot and loud. My plants don't mind.
gangsters&fall: Harvest time even in the city. Rooftops full of pumpkins.
gangsters&winter: Winter's slow. I'm planning next year's rows on paper.
eve: Festival tomorrow. I'm polishing my turnip. Yes, really.
birthday: You remembered my birthday? That's lovely. Come by the farm, I'll show you the lambs.
sun: Heat wave. I water at dawn and again at dusk, and the plants still sulk.
leaves: Leaves everywhere. I rake them into the compost. Next spring's soil.

always: Flour on my nose? Probably. It's always there.
A warm loaf fixes most things. The rest needs two.
If you bring me berries, I'll make you something you'll remember.
fall: Pumpkin pies all month. I've stopped counting.
Pumpkin pies, apple cakes, ginger biscuits. Fall is a baker's dream.
The bakery smells like cinnamon all fall. People just come in to breathe.
winter: Spiced bread in winter. My gran's recipe. Secret ingredient: more spice.
Frostberry tarts this week. They taste like cold, in a good way.
Winter baking keeps the kitchen warm. I don't mind the snow at all.
morning: I bake at dawn. The whole street smells like bread by six.
Still warm. Smell that? That's seven o'clock.
evening: Up at four, asleep by eight. Talk fast.
spring: Strawberry tarts the minute the first ones ripen. Bring me a basket and I'll bring you a tart.
Spring flowers on every cake this week. People keep asking for more.
Rhubarb's in! Rhubarb everything. I'm unstoppable.
summer: Too hot to proof dough after noon. I bake early and nap after lunch.
Too hot for the oven. I bake at four in the morning now.
Summer berries on everything. My fingers are purple.
rain: Rainy days sell more bread. Nobody wants to cook when it's pouring.
fog: Fog makes the bread rise slow. I talk to it. It doesn't help, but I talk to it.
penguins: A penguin tried to buy a bun with a pebble this morning. I gave it the bun.
gangsters: People who sit by the window with their backs to the wall tip very well. I don't ask.
f:shop_1_returned: I'm back. The ovens are back. Somebody paid for that, and I know who. Thank you.
The arcade kids still come by for day-old rolls. Some things I'll keep.
festival_egg: Egg-shaped buns, all day. I'm going to dream about eggs.
festival_star: Spiced loaf for every gift basket. My kitchen looks like a snowstorm.
festival_harvest: I've baked for the whole festival. My arms will never recover.
I've baked for the whole Harvest Fair. My arms will never recover.
festival_lantern: Lantern cakes! Little paper cups with a candle on top. Don't eat the candle.
gangsters&spring: Spring on the block. Fresh bread smells better than exhaust. Come in.
gangsters&summer: Hot ovens, hot street. I sell more cold buns than hot ones.
gangsters&fall: Pumpkin bread's back. The whole block lines up for it.
gangsters&winter: Snow outside, ovens inside. My bakery's the warmest shop on the street.
eve: Festival tomorrow! I've been up since three. I'll be up since three again tomorrow.
birthday: My birthday! I baked my own cake. I always do. It's the best one.
sun: Heat wave. My icing's melting faster than I can pipe it.

always: Quiet steps, {name}. The woods hear everything.
Wolves keep to the hills unless something drives them down. Lately, something has.
I take what the woods drop and no more. The forest notices greed.
Tracks don't lie. People do. That's why I like tracks.
winter: Easy tracking in snow. Hard everything else.
Fresh snow tells you everything. Who walked where, and when.
Pond's frozen at the edges. Safe only near the reeds.
fall: The deer are fattening up for winter. I just watch. They know I just watch.
Fall's the season for tracking. Soft ground, fewer leaves on the trees.
Geese are heading south. I watch them every year.
morning: Dew shows every track. Best hour of the day.
gangsters: Tracks by the south gate. City shoes. Two pairs, walking like they're paid to.
heat: You've got a tail. City boots, no patience. Lose him in the orchard.
spring: Spring tracks everywhere. Everything's out looking for breakfast.
Spring tracks are everywhere. Everything's moving again.
Fawns in the woods this time of year. Keep your distance.
summer: Hot days, the woods go quiet at noon. I do too.
Summer, the woods are thick. Hard to track, easy to get lost.
Long days for walking the ridge. I'll be back by dark. Probably.
festival_egg: I'll find every egg in the hunt. It's tracking. With eggs.
festival_lantern: Lanterns scare the owls. I'll watch from the trees.
festival_harvest: I don't enter the fair. I just eat. That's my contribution.
festival_star: Star Festival. Clear night for it. You can see every constellation.
gangsters&spring: Spring on the block. More feet on the street, harder to track.
gangsters&summer: Summer nights I walk the rooftops. Quiet up there.
gangsters&fall: Fall fog. Good for watching. Bad for being watched.
gangsters&winter: Snow on the street. Every footprint's a story.
eve: Festival tomorrow. Too many people. I'll go anyway.
birthday: Birthday. Nobody usually knows. ...Thanks.
snow: Fresh snow. Look: fox tracks, right across the plaza.

always: When I'm mayor, the fountain will be lemonade. Write that down.
I climbed the bell tower once. ONE time. Nobody lets me forget it.
I'm nine and three quarters. The quarters count.
Do you need an assistant? I'm very assisting.
festival: I'm in charge of the festival! Well. I'm in charge of the balloons. Some balloons.
evening: Mum says bed at eight. I say bed at eight-ish.
spring: Spring means puddles. Puddles mean jumping. That's science.
Spring! I found a bird's nest. I'm not touching it. I'm just guarding it.
I'm growing a bean in a cup at school. It's winning.
summer: Summer holidays! No school! Mum still makes me sweep the shop.
NO SCHOOL. All summer. I'm going to the pond every single day.
I got sunburnt on my nose. Mum says it's a souvenir.
fall: I'm collecting the best leaves. Only the red ones. The yellow ones are boring.
Back to school. I'm not sad. I'm a little sad.
I jumped in a leaf pile and found a sock. Not mine.
winter: I built a snow-mayor. It looks more like the mayor than the mayor does.
Snowball fight after school! You can be on my team.
I made a snowman. He's called Mr. Buttons. He's very tall.
festival_egg: I know where three eggs are. I'm not telling. Okay, one. No.
festival_star: I wrapped Mum's present myself. You can tell.
festival_lantern: My lantern has a star on it. It's floating the best.
festival_harvest: I'm entering the pumpkin contest. Mine's small but it's very round.
gangsters&summer: No school all summer. I'm running the hydrant on our corner.
gangsters&winter: Snow day! Nobody's on the street. Except me. And my sled.
eve: Festival TOMORROW. I can't sleep. I'm not even tired.
birthday: It's my BIRTHDAY. I'm this many now. Guess how many. MORE.
fireflies: Fireflies! I caught one and let it go. It said thank you. I think.
snow: SNOW DAY! No school! Come to the park, we're building a fort.

always: I found a frog with spots! I named it Spots. It's a good name.
Mum says I can't keep frogs in the kitchen. She didn't say anything about the bathtub.
Frogs sing at night if it's warm. Have you heard them?
I'm going to be a frog scientist. Or a potion-maker. Or both, for frogs.
spring: Tadpoles in the pond! Hundreds! I counted to forty and then they moved.
Tadpoles in the pond! I named all of them Frederick.
Spring rain brings out the frogs. Best season ever.
summer: Summer frogs are LOUD. I love it.
The pond's warm in summer. The frogs love it. So do I.
No school means more time with the frogs.
fall: The frogs are getting sleepy. I tucked one in. It didn't want to be tucked.
The frogs are getting sleepy. They'll hide in the mud soon.
Leaves on the pond look like little boats.
winter: Frogs sleep under the pond all winter. I check on them anyway.
The frogs are asleep under the ice. I whisper to them.
I built a snow frog. It's very big and very froggy.
festival_egg: I hid a frog in the egg basket. Don't tell. It wanted to see the festival.
festival_lantern: I made a frog lantern. It floats. Frogs float. Mostly.
festival_harvest: I entered a frog in the fair. They said no frogs. I said why. They didn't know.
festival_star: Star Festival. I wished for a frog that glows. Maybe next year.
eve: Festival tomorrow! My frog is very excited. Can't you tell?
birthday: It's my birthday! I'm going to the pond to tell the frogs.
snow: Snow day! I made a snow frog by the school gate.
fireflies: The fireflies are like frogs that glow. Flying frogs. I want one.

always: My kite went over the lighthouse yesterday. Marlowe gave it back. Again.
I collect shells. This one's my best. Don't touch it, look with your eyes.
If you hold a shell to your ear you hear the sea. Or your ear. Nobody's sure.
The wind's good today. Good for kites, bad for hats.
summer: Summer wind is the best kite wind. Everyone knows that.
No school! I'm working at the inn. Bram pays me in pie.
Summer, the inn's busy every night. I carry plates.
winter: Snow day! There's no school but I'm calling it a snow day.
Snow day! Bram let me light the fire. Well, hand him the match.
Bram says winter stew is the best stew. I've had three bowls to check.
spring: Spring tides bring the best shells. I've got a whole bucket.
I'm helping Bram plant herbs behind the inn. Mostly I dig holes.
Spring cleaning at the inn. I found three spoons under the stairs.
fall: Fall wind takes my kite all the way to the lighthouse. Marlowe waves.
Back to school. I miss carrying plates.
Fall, Bram makes soup every day. I've tasted every batch. For quality.
festival_harvest: Festival day! Bram let me carry the big pot. Well. One handle.
Bram let me carry the big pot. Well. One handle.
festival_egg: Egg Festival! I'm carrying the egg baskets. Very carefully.
festival_lantern: I'm helping light the lanterns. Bram says I have steady hands.
festival_star: I wrapped a present for Bram. It's a spoon. He needs more spoons.
eve: Festival tomorrow! I've polished every pot at the inn.
birthday: It's my birthday! Bram made me a pie. With my name on it. In pastry.
snow: Snow day! School's shut. I'm helping Bram shovel. Mostly I throw it.
sun: Too hot to carry plates. I'm carrying ice instead.

always: I press flowers in my diary. This one's from the meadow. Don't tell anyone it's my diary.
Some flowers only open at night. I've seen them. Mostly.
I'm writing down everything that happens in town. You're in it. Page twelve.
Daisies mean innocence. Dandelions mean I was bored.
spring: Spring is when the diary gets heavy. All the flowers.
Spring entry: the cherry trees are pink. Also: Pip fell in the pond.
I'm writing a poem about spring. It rhymes with thing. Most things do.
summer: Summer flowers go floppy by noon. I press them early.
Summer entry: hot. Very hot. Iced tea helps.
I'm writing my diary in the shade. The sun makes the ink run.
fall: Fall flowers are the brave ones. Page thirty-one is all asters.
Fall entry: leaves, pumpkins, school again. Mixed feelings.
Fall's my favourite season to write about. Everything's changing.
winter: No flowers in winter, so I press snowflakes. They don't keep.
Winter entry: snow, cocoa, Pip lost a mitten. Again.
I'm writing by the fire. My diary's almost full. I'll need a new one by spring.
festival: I'm writing the whole festival in my diary. You're on page forty.
festival_egg: Egg Festival entry: I found two. Pip found none. That's going in the diary.
festival_lantern: Lantern Festival. I wrote a wish on my lantern. It's private.
festival_harvest: Harvest Fair entry: pies, ribbons, Theo counting everything.
festival_star: Star Festival. I'm writing down everyone's gifts. For the record.
eve: Festival tomorrow. I've saved a whole page for it.
birthday: My birthday! I'm writing it in my diary in gold pen.
snow: Snow day entry: no school, three snowmen, one lost mitten.
leaves: Leaf entry: I pressed twelve leaves in my diary. It's thicker now.

always: Thirty years I kept that lamp. Mostly by myself.
Storm or calm, the sea's always talking. You just have to sit long enough.
Gulls are terrible company and I'd miss them dreadfully.
The boy from the inn keeps flying his kite into my gallery. I keep giving it back. It's a system.
rain: Weather like this, the lamp's the only thing that matters.
not:lighthouse_lit: Ships haven't come in a while. I'd light it anyway, if it had oil. Habit, or hope.
if:lighthouse_lit: Lamp's lit. Fish come up to look at it after dark, fools that they are.
A boat came round the point last night. First in years. It waved. I waved. Neither of us knew what to do after that.
I polish that lens every morning now. It's the best part of the day.
winter: Fog season. The bell and I have long talks.
fall: Gulls are fattening up for winter. So am I.
gangsters: Lamp sees the whole coast. Including the boats that don't want to be seen.
if:lighthouse_lit&night: Look at the water. That's the lamp, out there, coming back.
spring: Spring storms come in sideways. The lamp room hums all night.
summer: Long days. The lamp barely earns its keep.

always: Stone's honest. You hit it right, it breaks right.
The quarry's deeper than it looks. Mind the edges.
Coal, copper, iron, stone, brick. If it's heavy, I sell it.
My golems are long gone. The crew carved them to lift stone, and one spring they just walked off into the mountain.
winter: Cold stone splits easier. Silver lining.
gangsters: Somebody's been buying dynamite with cash and no questions. I ask questions. They stopped buying.
spring: Thaw loosens the cut. Mind your step on the north face.
summer: Summer sun bakes the quarry floor. Bring water. Bring more than that.
fall: Good dry stone in the fall. Best building season there is.

always: These runes are older than the town. Older than the valley, maybe.
Every ruin is a sentence. I'm still learning the grammar.
The deeper you go, the older the stories get.
I came here for a week, four years ago.
penguins: The star that fell here didn't fall by accident. The ruins say it was sent.
gangsters: A man from the city offered to buy my tablets. Every one. I said they weren't for sale. He said everything is.
spring: Spring rain washes new runes out of the mud. Every year, a few more.
winter: Frost shows the carvings sharper. Cold, but worth it.

always: The marsh keeps its own time. Don't rush it.
Mushrooms and moss, mud and mist. Everything I need.
Visitors are rare. Tea? It's mostly marsh. Mostly.
The frogs told me you were coming. They tell me everything.
rain: Rain? Out here we just call it the usual.
spring: Marsh wakes up loud. Frogs have opinions.
summer: Summer marsh. The air's thick enough to chew.
fall: Mushroom season. The good ones and the other ones. Ask before you pick.
winter: Winter marsh sleeps. I sleep too, mostly sitting up.

always: Sheep are smarter than people think. Not smart. Smarter.
The orchard's best in late summer. Come pick something.
Wool today, jumpers tomorrow. That's the whole business.
My dog does the real work. I just carry the snacks.
fall: Apple season! Pick a basket for the market before the wasps do.
spring: Lambing time. I sleep in the barn with a lantern and a lot of patience.
summer: Shearing done. The flock looks like startled clouds.
winter: Snow on the hills. The sheep don't mind. I mind for all of us.
rain: Wet wool smells like wet wool. There's no poetry in it.
gangsters: Folk in good shoes come up here sometimes. They don't stay. Hills are hard on good shoes.

always: Measure twice, cut once. Then sand it till it purrs.
Every chair in {town} has a wobble I know by name.
New pieces come off the bench every few days. Come look before somebody else does.
Good timber tells you where it wants to split. Listen and it won't fight you.
spring: Spring's for garden benches. Everyone wants to sit outside the second it stops raining.
Spring repairs. Every fence in town needs a nail.
New planks for the bridge this spring. Sal's watching me like a hawk.
summer: Wood moves in the heat. I leave every joint a hair loose in summer.
Building stalls for the summer markets. Hammer, saw, repeat.
Too hot in the workshop. I build outside under the tree.
fall: Wood's dry this time of year. Best season to build.
Fall's for roofs. Fix them before the snow, not after.
Building harvest crates for Hazel. Dozens of them.
winter: Winter's for beds and chairs. People notice their furniture when they're stuck indoors.
Winter, I build furniture. Indoor work for indoor weather.
Sledges! Every kid in town wants one fixed this week.
rain: Damp air, swollen drawers. Half the town will be at my door by tomorrow.
wind: Wind took a sheet of ply clean off the bench. If you find it, it's mine.
evening: Sawdust in my hair, soup in my bowl. Good day.
penguins: Something small and round sat on my sawhorse this morning. It looked very pleased with itself.
gangsters: The crews let me be. Everybody needs a table, even people who sit with their backs to the door.
festival: I built the stall frames for today. If one wobbles, tell me before you tell anyone else.
festival_harvest: My pie's on the table. I made the table too. Judge them separately.
festival_egg: I built the egg hunt hiding spots. Some of them are very clever.
festival_lantern: I built the lantern launch on the water. It floats. I tested it. Twice.
festival_star: I built the star frame for the tree. It's very sturdy. Climb it at your peril.
eve: Festival tomorrow. Stall frames are up. Don't lean on them yet.
birthday: My birthday! I made myself a new chair. Come sit in it.

always: Cat-topia welcomes careful visitors. Careless ones get a stern look.
A bell is just copper that has learned to sing. Remember that.
winter: Cat-topia does not do cold. Cat-topia does blankets.
rain: Rain. Every cat in the meadow is indoors and offended.
